subject: Lumencare: Marketplace alignment runbook & PO acceptance path
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumencare.ai>; Priya Desai <priya.desai@lumencare.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace alignment runbook & PO acceptance path

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As promised I pulled together a concise runbook that stitches together the evaluation milestones, the private-offer acceptance path for AWS Marketplace, and the billing cadence options your finance team asked about. I attached the draft MAP (lumencare-mvp-eval-plan.xlsx) and an internal copy of the AWS private-offer draft.

High-level items in this runbook:
- Evaluation gates (functional smoke tests, performance SLA check, canary workload).
- AWS private offer acceptance steps (Marketplace PO -> Provider acceptance -> Cloud vendor invoice flow).
- Billing options: metered consumption vs commit+true-up; recommended for pilot: 3-month commit with monthly metered true-up.
- Procurement asks from Lumencare (SOC 2 evidence, IP & data handling clause redlines, KMS keyflow for customer-managed keys).

Can we lock the following dates to keep momentum?
1) Formal evaluation kickoff: Tue Aug 13 (Redwood to provide test tenants + workload script)
2) Legal review pass-back: Wed Aug 21
3) Procurement PO submission target: Mon Aug 27

Next steps from our side: Karthik will send the technical acceptance checklist and a sample billing schedule; Laura will replicate the runbook into your shared Drive folder so your procurement team can comment.

If that schedule works, I’ll convert the attached MAP into the HubSpot mutual-action task list and invite the procurement contact.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu | Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0167

Attachments: lumencare-mvp-eval-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), aws-private-offer-draft.pdf (PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@lumencare.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Aug 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace alignment runbook & PO acceptance path

Thanks Jasmine — quick technical notes to seed the eval plan.

Summary of acceptance gates I added to the sheet:
- Connectivity: VPC peering or PrivateLink proof-of-connection within 48h of kickoff.
- Key management: confirm KMS ownership model (Lumencare CMK vs Redwood-managed envelope keys).
- Latency check: 95th percentile < 120ms for the sample inference pipeline (6k tokens / sec peak) during canary.
- Billing telemetry: our SDK provides token-level cost logs; will need an S3 delivery or partner BI pull for your finance.

Notes for procurement: AWS private-offer flow has two acceptance triggers — provider accepts offer in Marketplace, and then AWS issues the invoice to Lumencare. If you need invoice-on-redwood (vendor invoice to Lumencare), we'll need an off-marketplace reseller arrangement which adds ~2 weeks to procurement.

I attached a short checklist in the Drive link for Laura to drop into the MAP sheet.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Priya Desai <priya.desai@lumencare.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@lumencare.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace alignment runbook & PO acceptance path

Thanks, Jasmine & Karthik —

This looks good. A few clarifications from procurement before we lock dates:
- We prefer vendor-invoiced billing (Lumencare receives invoice from Redwood) rather than AWS-issued invoices for the pilot; please confirm if Redwood can accommodate that.
- For legal: can you provide SOC 2 Type II report and a short KMS integration note that our security team can slot into the SOW?
- Can you confirm the total committed amount for the 3-month pilot (we need an exact number for the internal PO).

If you can answer those three items by EOD Wed Aug 14 our procurement lead will prepare the PO and target submission for Aug 27 as suggested.

Best,
Priya Desai
Head of Procurement | Lumencare Health AI
procurement@lumencare.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@lumencare.ai>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Aug 2029 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace alignment runbook & PO acceptance path

Hi Priya —

Quick answers inline and a few attachments dropped into the shared Drive link.

- Vendor-invoiced billing: Redwood can issue vendor invoices rather than AWS-originated invoices. That requires a short billing addendum (billing-terms-summary.docx attached) and billing contact confirmation (name + remit address). Choosing vendor-invoiced flow will add ~5 business days to the acceptance timeline (we'll lock the PO in our vendor system and then accept the private offer on AWS).

- SOC 2: attaching our SOC 2 Type II summary and a bridge letter; full report available under NDA.

- Committed amount for the 3-month pilot: $45,000 (this is our recommended commit number to cover baseline throughput with the agreed canary profile). We can provide a pro-rated invoice schedule if you prefer monthly true-ups.

Action items:
1) Priya — confirm billing contact + remit address (needed for addendum).
2) Procurement team — if you want vendor invoicing, note the extra 5 business days and we’ll plan acceptance accordingly.
3) Jasmine — move the MAP tasks to HubSpot and invite procurement.

Ben, can you sign off on the vendor-invoice addendum draft and loop legal if redlines show up?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett | Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: billing-terms-summary.docx, SOC2-summary.pdf
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Desai <priya.desai@lumencare.ai>, Procurement Team <procurement@lumencare.ai>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Aug 2029 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace alignment runbook & PO acceptance path

Priya / Lumencare procurement —

Ben here, I’ll own the vendor-invoice route and the addendum. Quick summary and final recommendation:

1) If you want Redwood to invoice Lumencare directly: we will issue Net 30 invoices to the billing contact once the PO is accepted and the pilot begins. Expect an additional ~5 business days in the timeline to complete vendor onboarding on our side.
2) If you choose AWS-issued invoices (Marketplace native): acceptance is quicker but invoices come from AWS. This path is simpler for your procurement operations but complicates reconciliation on our end.

Recommendation: go vendor-invoiced for organizational clarity (we’ll do the extra onboarding) — this keeps the billing relationship between Redwood and Lumencare and simplifies future renewals/credits.

If Lumencare confirms vendor-invoiced billing and provides remit details by EOD Wed Aug 14, we will:
- Finalize the billing addendum and return it for signature by Fri Aug 16.
- Begin vendor onboarding so we can accept the AWS private offer immediately on PO receipt (target PO receipt Aug 27 remains achievable).

Happy to hop on a 15-min call today if that helps speed the billing contact confirmation.

—Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
